raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so I cannot spread myself too thin. This year I will still keep the old pattern that feels safest for my family: 2 mu in wheat-maize rotation, 1 mu in cotton. Wheat and maize give me grain and steady cash, and cotton is slower but sometimes sells better, so keeping all three is my way to avoid putting everything on one crop. Some people say put more land into cotton when price looks decent, but with family members working outside and only limited labor at home, I do not want too much hand work at picking time.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, with a local improved variety that people here use a lot. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once at jointing. The extension guy says do not push nitrogen too hard, but if wheat looks pale in spring, I still add a bit because too little fertilizer hurts yield more than spending a little extra. I have a well, so I plan around 3 irrigations for wheat if rainfall is normal: once before winter or after sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once around grain filling if needed. After wheat harvest in June, the maize must go in quickly. That turnaround is always tight, so I will do simple rotary tillage or even just light field prep and sow maize fast. For maize I will use hybrid seed, put most fertilizer at planting, then one topdress around knee-high stage. If rain is decent I may irrigate only once, because pumping water costs money.

For the 1 mu cotton, I will keep input moderate. Cotton can make money, but on a small plot I cannot afford to chase very high yield with heavy fertilizer and many sprays. I will sow in mid-April, use a common improved cotton seed from the township market, put base fertilizer first, then topdress in stages if the stand looks good. Cotton needs more watching for insects than wheat or maize, so I will spray only when I really see pressure. This year my thinking is simple: stable yield first, spending carefully second, and no big changes unless weather or prices force me.
